en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Maidens (Kumāribhūtavagga).
73. The Third Training Rule Concerning Maidens.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, nuns were giving the full admission to a maiden who was twenty years of age and had trained for two years in the six rules, yet who had not been authorized by the Saṅgha.
The nuns said to her:
"Come, trainee; find this out, give this, bring this, there is need of this, and make this allowable."
They replied, “We are not trainees, noble lady; we are bhikkhunīs.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before]... were indignant, complained, and spread it about:
“How can nuns give the full admission to a maiden who is twenty years of age, who has trained for two years in the six rules, yet has not been authorized by the Saṅgha?

… [The Buddha asked: “Is it true, monks, that nuns are giving the full admission to a maiden who is twenty years of age, who has trained for two years in the six rules, yet has not been authorized by the Saṅgha?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How, monks, can these bhikkhunīs give the full admission to a maiden who is twenty years of age, who has trained for two years in the six rules, yet has not been authorized by the Saṅgha?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of those with faith…” [and so on].
Having rebuked them … and having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks,
I allow you to grant the formal consent for ordination to a maiden who is twenty years of age and has trained in the six rules for two years.”
And furthermore, monks, it should be given in this way:
that girl who has reached twenty years of age and has trained for two years in the six rules should approach the Saṅgha,
arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, pay homage at the feet of the bhikkhunīs, and squat down.
Having sat down and raised her joined palms in reverence, she should speak thus:
“Venerable ladies, I, so-and-so, who am twenty years of age and have been a maiden for two years, having trained in the six rules, request the Saṅgha’s permission for full admission.
She should request it a second time as well.
A third time she should be asked.
A competent and capable bhikkhunī should inform the Saṅgha:
"Let the noble Saṅgha listen to me.
This woman, [name], who is twenty years of age, a maiden, and who has trained for two years in the six rules under the noble lady [name], requests the Saṅgha for permission to go forth.
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha grant permission to go forth to this woman, [name], who is twenty years of age, a maiden, and who has trained for two years in the six rules.
This is the motion.
"Let the Sangha, noble ladies, hear me.

This woman named so-and-so, having reached twenty years of age, being a maiden, and having trained for two years in the six rules under the noble lady named so-and-so, requests formal admission from the Sangha.
The Sangha grants formal admission to this woman named so-and-so, who has reached twenty years of age, being a maiden, and has trained for two years in the six rules."

Whichever noble lady approves of granting the authorization for ordination to the maiden named so-and-so, who is twenty years of age and has trained in the training in the six rules for two years, let her remain silent;
whichever does not approve, let her speak.
The Sangha has granted the authorization for ordination to the maiden named so-and-so, who is twenty years of age and has trained in the training in the six rules for two years.
“The Saṅgha consents, therefore it is silent; thus do I understand this.

Then the Blessed One, having rebuked those bhikkhunīs in many ways for being difficult to support … [as before] … “And furthermore, bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule as follows:”

“Whatever nun should give the full admission to a maiden who is twenty years of age, who has trained for two years in the six rules, but who has not been authorized by the Saṅgha, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun... [and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"One who has reached twenty years of age" means:
"Having reached twenty years of age.
"A maiden" refers to a female novice (sāmaṇerī).
"Two years" means two full years.
"One who has trained in the training" means:
Those who have trained in the six rules.
"Not authorized" means that the authorization for rehabilitation has not been granted by means of a formal act consisting of a motion and a second.
"Should give the going forth" means:
she should confer full ordination.
If, thinking "I will give the going forth," she seeks out a group, a preceptor, a bowl, or a robe, or if she demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For the motion, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For the two formal proclamations, there are offenses of wrong-doing.
At the conclusion of the formal proclamation, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya) for the preceptor.
For the community and for the preceptor, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she gives the full admission in a formal act that is legitimate, perceiving it as legitimate, there is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
If she gives the full admission in a formal act that is legitimate, while being doubtful of it, there is an offense entailing expiation.
If it is a legitimate legal act (*dhammakamma*) and she perceives it as an illegitimate legal act (*adhammakamma*), yet she ordains her, there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
If it is an illegitimate legal act and she perceives it as a legitimate legal act, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
If it is an illegitimate legal act and she is uncertain, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one perceives it as such, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense if she ordains a girl who has reached twenty years of age, who has trained for two years in the six rules, and who has been approved by the Saṅgha.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of a first-offender.
The third training rule is concluded.
